p.seg: whoever reads my poems
must guard his purity of heart
his greed at once be modesty
flattery suddenly honesty
banish and be rid of evil karma
trust and accept his true nature
get his buddha body today
hurry as if these were orders
storied cliffs were the furtune I cast [I chose storied cliffs for my abode CH]
bird trails beyond human tracks
what surround my yard
white clouds nesting dark rocks
I've lived here quite a few years
and always seen the spring-winter change
tell those people with tripods and bells
empty names are no damn good
funny the road to Cold Mountain
no track of cart or horse
hard to mark which merging stream
or know which piled-up ridge
a jungle of plants weeps [weeping dew are all kinds of grass/weeds CH]
a forest of pine sighs [murmuring in the wind is one kind of pine CH]
and now where the trails is lost
form asks shadow where to
give me a hidden eddy [I prefer to live in hiding CH]
a residence free from dust and noise
trampled grass for my path [I trample down grass and this becomes my scholar's retreat. CH]
overhead clouds as neighbors [I look up at the clouds and they become my neighbours. CH]
birds to help me sing
no one asking about Dharma
this Saha tree nowadays
has springs of how many years [counts several years as one spring.]
zither and scroll are up to you
but money and power are vain
leave the carriage heed the wise wife
in the covered cart is a pious son
wind blows across threshing floors
water spills from hatchery pools
keep in mind the tailorbird
at home on a single branch
brothers share five prefectures
father and sons three provinces
to see how flying ducks flock
roam under the white hare banner
receive the magic melon in a dream
take sacred citrons from the throne
so far away from your native land
lodge with fish in a stream
a wielder of scroll and sword
three times met wise lords
on watch in the east his letters unfavored
on march in the west his arms unhonored
he studied letters and studied arms
studied arms and studied letters
today now that he's old
what's left isn't worth saying
Chuangtze spoke of his funeral
Heaven and Earth are my coffins
whenever I come to that
all I'll need is a shroud
dead I'll feed green flies
won't bother white cranes to mourn
starve on Shou Yang Mountain [As I am starving at Shouyang Mountain (like Bo Yi etc) CH]
living honest dying's fine too [living honestly, dying is also a pleasure. CH]
people ask the way to Cold Mountain
roads don't reach Cold Mountain
summer the ice never melts
sunup the fog is thick
how did someone like me arrive
our minds aren't the same
if they were [If you, my reader, are like me in your mind CH]
you could get there then [you could still get there (although there are no roads) CH]
heaven's own giant trees
get cut into planks [long planks CH]
helpless building timber
is left in an unsunned valley
many years its heart still strong
long days its bark becomes bare
let an old hand take it away [bring it here, fetch it]
it still can prop up a stable
I spur my horse past ruins
ruins move a traveller's heart
the old parapets high and low
the ancient graves large and small
the shuddering shadow of a tumbleweed
the steady sound of great trees
but what I lament are the common bones
all unamed in the records of the immortals
parrots dwell in western lands
the nets of foresters bring them back
beauties tease them dawn to dusk
back and forth behind courtyard curtains
they're given a golden cage [they are given the privilege to be put in a golden cage CH]
but locked up lose their plumes
or like wild geese and swans [They are not as fine as the wild swans and the cranes,
soaring into the clouds [who soar up, enter the clouds and fly off. CH]
in Jade Hall hangs a curtain of pearls
within is a graceful girl
her looks shame the immortals
complexion like a peach or plum
in the east spring mists gather
in the west fall wind stirs
another thirty years pass
she ends up chewed sugar cane
a moth-browed girl in the city
how her pendants chime
plays with a parrot before the flowers
plucks a lute beneath the moon
her arias echo three months
ten thousand see her briefest dance
she won't be like this long
the lotus can't bear cold
my parents' endeavors were many
I don't covet others' fields and groves
my wife works her loom clack clack
our baby his mouth gu gu
I clap and urge the flowers to dance
prop up my chin and listen to birds
but who comes to commend me
woodcutters often come by
living below green cliffs
I don't mow anymore weeds
new vines hang in spirals
old rocks stand in spires
monkeys pick the mountain fruit
egrets spear the fish in the pools
one or two scrolls of the immortals
I mumble under the trees
the seasons never rest
a year leaves and a year arrives
creatures take their turns
the Heavens don't decay
the east gets bright the west gets dark
flowers fall and blossom again
only travellers to the Yellow Springs
disappear and don't return
the year goes trading a year of sorrow
spring comes and colors are fresh
mountain flowers laugh with green water
cliff trees dance with blue mist
bees and butterflies say they're happy
birds and fishes lovelier still
companions in love
can't sleep through dawn
handwriting so unrestrained
physique robust enough
alive a body with limits
dead a ghost without name
it's been like this since long ago
what can you do now
you can come into the clouds
I'll teach you magic mushroom songs
looking for a refuge
Cold Mountain will keep you safe
a faint wind stirs dark pines
come closer the sound gets better
below them a gray-haired man
mumbles Huang and Lao
ten years unable to return
he's forgotten the way he came
a handsome boy on a horseback
waves his whip at the willows
can't imagine doomsday
makes no boat or ladder
each season's flowers are fine
then one day turn withered and brown
rock honey and clarified butter
you can't taste dead
a man who dines on sunsets
shunned the usual haunts for a home
any season it's truly dead
in summer just like fall
a dark gorge always babbles
a towering pine wind sighs
he sits there half a day
a forgets a lifetime of sorrow
your maid's lived in Han Tan
her singing has the lilt
make use of her refuge
this song has long been long
you're drunk don't talk of going
stay the day's not done
where you sleep tonight
her quilt fills a silver bed
pole your three winged galleons
ride your thousand-mile stallions
you still won't reach my home
it's called the darkest wild
cliff cave deep in the mountains
clouds and thunder come down all day
I'm not Master Confucius
I have nothing to offer others
wise ones you ignore me
I ignore you fools
neither wise nor foolish
don't hear of me henceforth
at night I'll sing to the moon
at dawn I'll dance with the clouds
how can I stop my mouth and hands
and sits up straight with all this hair
the bird of five colors
that rest in the paulownia and eats bamboo seeds
moves slowly with dignity
and sings in the light or dark scale
why did it finally come
appearing before me awhile
whenever it hears strings and singing
it dances while it can
thatch and beam are a hick's residence
before his door carts and horses are few
the forest is dark but partial to birds
the streams are wide and native to fish
he takes his son to pick mountain fruit
with his wife hoes fertile fields
what does he have inside
just a bed full of books
Climbing Cold Mountain Road
Cold Mountain Road doesn't end
the streams are long and piled with rocks
the gorges wide and choked with grass
the moss is slick without any rain
the pines sing without the wind
who can get past the tangles of the world
and sit with me in the clouds
with whom the six ends entangle
you bring up the nine knots in vain
the talented leave the weeds and swamps
the unskilled close grass doors
when the sun is high the cliffs are still dark
when the mist is gone the valleys are still dim
inside are the sons of elders
and none of them have any shorts
where white clouds are high rugged crags
and green water rolling dark waves
I hear a fisherman
again and again his song at the oars
beat after beat I can't listen
it brings me too much sorrow
who said sparrows don't have horns
how else could they pierce my hut
Cold Mountain Road is aloof
Cold Gorge Shore is unfriendly
birds chatter away
nobody else it's dead
gusts of wind turn my face
flurries of snow bury me
day after day I don't see the sun
year after year I don't know spring
what makes a young man grieve
he grieves to see his temples white
besides white what makes him grieve
he grieves to see the day crowd near
he goes to dwell on T'ai Shan
he's sent to stay on Pei Mang
how do I bear to speak these words
these words hurt an old man
I've heard that cares are hard to dispel
a saying I thought untrue
but yesterday what I drove off
entangles me again today
moons wane but not cares
the year is now but cares are newer
who'd guess beneath the big hat
is really a man of old cares
to turtles were aboard an ox cart
when a roadside drama occured
a scorpion came alongside
begging desperately for a ride
or refuse would violate good will
to accept would weigh them down
in a finger snap I couldn't describe
acting kindly they got stung
the Third Moon silkworms still small
girls come gathering flowers
chasing butterflies by the wall
throwing at frogs beside the river
stuffing plums into sheer silk sleeves
digging up bamboo shoots with gold lancets
wrangle about what's fine
this place outdoes mine
an old lady to the east
got rich a few years ago
before poorer than me
she laughs that I'm broke
she laughs that I'm behind
I laugh that she's ahead
we laugh like we won't stop
form the east and from the west
a rich man is so occupied
he can't just acquiesce
his granary rice already bright red
he won't loan a peck or a quart
he turns his thoughts to guile
buying coarse silk he picks the best
whenever he reaches his final day
for mourners there'll be flies
I once beheld a brilliant man
learned and shrewd without peer
his fine name on top resounded the realm
his five-word line surpassed all others'
as an officer his ministry excelled his predecessors'
he thought he couldn't follow the dust in back
suddenly rich and honored he took to wealth and beauty
when tiles break or ice melts you can't show them off
the white crane carries a bitter flower
a thousand miles before resting
he's bound for the peaks of P'eng Lai
with this for his provision
not yet there his feathers break off
far from the flock he grieves
returning to his old nest
his wife and children don't know him
ususally I live in seclusion
then I head for Kuo Ch'ing
sometimes to visit Feng Kan the Elder
sometimes to see Mister Shih
I go back up to Cold Cliff alone
an agreement we've never spoker
tracing a springless stream
the spring's dry but not the stream
if you were to dumb the life before
you won't be enlightened now
and such poverty as today's
is the work of previous lives
don't reform this life either
the next life will be the same
on both shores there's no ferry
it's far but you'll cross one day
the lustrous Lady Lu
has long been called Never Sad
she love to ride a flower-picking horse
she was happy poling a lily-gathering boat
she knelt on a green bear rug
and wore a blue phoenix robe
but grieved that in a hundred years
she couldn't help ending in the hills
Mistress Tsou of Ti Yen
and Mistress Tu of Han Tan
the two of them equally old
their love of face the same
yesterday went to a tea
but ill-dressed were shown to the back
because their skirts were frayed
they had to eat hardtack
beneath white cliffs I lie alone
streaming clouds don't fade all day
my hut might be dim
but my mind is free of noise
off dreaming I visited golden gates
my spirit returned when I crossed Stone Bridge
I left behind what burdened me
my dipper in the trees clack
things have their uses
and each use has its fit
if a use is out of place
there's a gap and a deficiency
a round hole and a square handle
is such a vain undertaking
a race horse to catch rats
will never match a lame cat
what person never dies
death has long been fair
as I recall a towering man
he's suddenly a pile of dust
the World Below has no dawn
the green grass has its spring
who comes to this heart-breaking place
the pine wind grieves to death
a black-maned roan and coral whip
fly down Lo Yang Road
a complacent handsome youth
doesn't expect old age
but white hair will surely appear
and red cheeks won't keep long
just look at Pei Mang Mountain
there's the Isle of Immortals
daylong they seem drunk
don't stop at all for years
buried beneath weeds
dawn must be dim
flesh and bones vanished completely
souls about withered away
notwithstanding iron-snapping jaws
helpless to chant the old sutras
once I got to Cold Mountain
I stayed thrity years
finally looking up family and friends
most had entered the Springs
slowly fading like a sputtering candle
or far flowing like a passing stream
this morning facing a solitary shadow
suddenly two tears welled
picking lotuses we called
the Clearwater was lovely
having fun we didn't feel dusk
we kept watching a wild wind stir
swells cradled the mandarin ducks
waves rocked the mallards
and us resting our oars
while our thoughts surged on and on
my mind is like the autumn moon
in a jade pool clear and bright
nothing can compare
tell me what to say
the hanging willow is dark like mist
its flying lowers drift like snow
man in a wife-forsaken province
wife in a man-missing county
each on one shore of the sky
when will they meet again
here's a message for moonlit towers
don't harbor pairs of swallows
call friends over when there's wine
call neighbors in when there's meat
bound for Yellow Springs
look alive while you're young and strong [young and strong, you should excert your efforts] [CA]
a jade belt's transient glory
gold hairpins aren't lasting charms
Old Man Chang and Old Lady Cheng
haven't sent back any news
a likeable fine fellow
physically imposing
not thirty springs and autumns
talents of a hundred kinds
his golden bridles chase noble guests
his jade dishes gather good friends
he only has one fault
he doesn't hand on the eternal lamp
peach blossoms would last through summer
but the wind and moon won't wait
look around for a man of the Han
not one of them stayed behind
day after day the petals drift down
year after year we move on
where we raise the dust today
was a great sea long ago
I saw a girl to the east
her years maybe eighteen
from the west men vied to propose
a willing match man and wife wed
stewing sheep and cooking a host of creatures
gathering for wantonness and slaughter
smiling and laughing merrily
receiving their judgement in treats
farmers with lots of mulberry groves
buffalo calves filling stables and ruts
willing to believe in cause and effect
the numbskulls crack sooner or later
their eyes see it all used up
then everyone on their own
paper pants and tiles for shorts
frozen and starved in the end
I see a hundred-odd dogs
every one of them scruffy
happy to lie by themselves
glad to ramble alone
but throw out a bone
and watch them growl and fight
because with bones so few
a pack of dogs can't share
long horizon-eyed gaze
white clouds all quarters unclear
owls and ravens fed and relaxed
phoenixes hungry and anxious
fine steeds are grazed in the gravel
lame donkeys allowed at court
Heaven's too high to hear
a tailorbird on the Blue
in Lo Yang so many girls
on a spring day show their charms
together pick roadside flowers
and stick them high in their hair
high in their hair the flowers wind round
someone sees and they all look down
looking elsewhere for gentle love
or going home to show husbands
in spring girls flaunt their looks
together along South Street
before the flowers grieving it's late
behind the trees dreading the wind
a young man comes alongside
a white horse and golden bridle
why must they flirt so long
their husbands know why
grirls play in the fading night
wind coes and the whole road's perfumed
sewn on skirts are butterflies of gold
stuck in hairdos are ducks of jade
young maids in red sheer silk
eunuchs in purple brocade
watching is someone who's lost his way
white temples and a trembling heart
whoever runs into a ghost or spirit
most of all don't be afraid
be firm don't try to grab it
call its name it'll will leave
with incense peitition the Buddha's power
bow down and seek a monk's aid
a mosquito that hammers an iron ox
has no place to sink its beak
the Yellow River overwhelms
flowing east without stopping
on and on never resting
while lives have an end
and if you would ride white clouds
how will you grow wings
unless while your hair's still black
you look alive moving or still
aboard this boat of rotten wood
gathering fruit of the nimba tree
I've journeyed to the open sea
where waves and swells never cease
only one night's food along
shore three thousand miles away
what's the cause of my distress
I'm grieved to say it's bitterness
stay dumb and make no sign
and what will have posterity have to tell
dwell hidden in woods and swamps
and how will your wisdom appear
withering isn't healthy
wind and frost bring early ills
a clay ox ploughing a field of rocks
has never had a harvest
it's so cold in the mountains
not just now but always
dim ridges eternally suck in snow
dark forests forever spray mist
plants grow after Grain Ears
leaves fall before Autumn Begins
and a long traveller here
peers without seeing the sky
a hermit's heart is heavy
he rues the shift of years
looks hard for roots and mushrooms
bur rummaging won't make him immortal
the court is wide the clouds just curling
the forest bright the moon just full
why doesn't he go back
cimmamon trees detain him
someone sits in a mountain gorge
cloud robe sunset tassles
handful of fragrances he'd share
the road is long and hard
regretful and doubtful
old and unaccomplished
the crowd calls him crippled
he stands alone steadfast
pigs eat dead human flesh
humans eat dead pig guts
pigs don't mind that humas stink
humans say pigs smell fine
throw dead pigs in the river
bury dead humans deep
when neather eats the other
lilies will bloom in boiling soups
Chaos was happy
it neither ate nor peed
whose drill did it meet
that fixed it with nine holes
day in working for food and clothes
year out worrying about rent and taxes
thousands fight for a coin
the crowd yells run for your life
what's this crying for
these tears as big as pearls
parting is certain
but mourning will return
and the reason that we're poor
we'll never fathom karma
shoulder the corpse to the mounds
the Six Paths don't please me
the wife got tired of weaving
the husband too lazy too hoe
lax and given to packing a bow
wearing slippers and fingering strings
for cold bones clothes are urgent
to fill up food comes first
who cares about you now
crying to the blue sky in pain
she doesn't travel the right road
strays but syas she's a laywoman
mouth seldom shamed before gods and buddhas
hearts always harboring jealousy
behind backs gobbles fish and meat
before others she chants Buddha
with self--improvement like this
how will she escape trouble
there's one sort of fool
as dense as a donkey
he understands human speech
his lust is more like a pig's
his treachery's hard to fathom
his statements turn out empty
whoever can talk to him
tell him don't live here
a man who's surnamed Pride
called Greedy and styled Dishonest
has no understanding whatever
all work he dispises
his mortal hatred is crowfoot
his vital love is honey
he eats fish as if he won't stop
and never grows tired of meat
go ahead live on rhino horn
wear tiger eyea if you want
break off a peach branch for medicine
use garlic peel for beads
warm your belly with dogwood wine
empty your mind with wedding-vine soup
you still have to die in the end
seeking long live is vain
I chose a secluded place
T'ien T'ai says it all
gibbons howl and the gorge fog's cold
a view of the peak adorns my grass door
bamboo leaves roof a pine hut
I cleared a pool and led in the spring
glad at last to put everything down
picking ferns I pass the years left
adding add to your essence
that could be called an addition
chaning change your form
that would be called change
able to add and able to change
you're sure to scale the Roll of Immortals
without addition and change
you won't avoid the crisis of death
vain labor repeating the Histories
an indulgence reading he Classics
checking yellow rolls until I'm old
recording plain people as usual
Continued Hardship was my lot
Emptiness and Danger rule my life
I can't match riverside trees
every year green awhile
spring waer is pure in an emerald gorge
moonlight white on Cold Mountain
silence thought and spirit becomes clear
behold space and the world grows still
I have a coat
neither sheer nor twilled silk
what color you ask
neither red nor purple
summer it serves as a shirt
winter it serves as a cape
winter and summer always in use
yearlong only this
white whisk and sandalwood handle
a perfume you smell all day
soft like curling fog
light like travelling clouds
for rites it's fine in summer
raised high it flicks dust away
and time after time in a ten-foot square
it's used to direct lost men
some people look for happiness in love
unaware there's misfortune in a hundred-year body
just look at a mirage or a bubble
and realize impermanence undoes us all
ut a grown man's will is straight like iron
in a uncrooked hear the Way is right
dense and tall bamboos beneath the frost
show you the mind 's not used in vain
there're so many kinds of people
a hundred plans for fame and profit
hearts greedy seeking glory
busy scheming riches and honors
minds that never rest
rushing around like smoke
dependents form a cricle
one yell and a hundred nods follow
in less that seventy years
ice melts and tiles breack apart
finally dead their affairs all cease
who will be their heirs
soak a mud ball in water
and you'll know thoughtless wisdom
a greedy man loves hoarding wealth
like an owl loves her chicks
the chicks grow up and eat their mother
wealth multiplies and swallows its owner
spread it and blessings grow
hoard it and disaster arises
no wealth no disaster
flap your wings in the blue
ten-thousand miles from home
sword raised to strike the Hun
gain the edge he's dead
lose it and you're doomed
you might not grudge his life
but why be ungrateful for yours
I'll tell you the art of victory
it's simply don't be greedy
anger is a fire in the mind
it can burn up a forest of merit
if you're travelling the bodhisattva's path
forbearance keeps anger away
you buried heads are senseless
preferring unlit demon caves
I've urged you often to straighten up
but your're stubborn and confused
unwilling to take Cold Mountain's advice
whirling fater karma's flux
until beheaded and you're in two
evil destinies cloud the eye
doubly dark and sunless
eight hundred years of man
wouldn't equal their half-night
all such fools as these
of states too sad to tell
I urge you try to leave
spot the King of Dharmas
Heaven is boundlessl high
Earth is endlessly deep
between are living things
supported by these Creators
knocking heads to be fed and warm
making plans to eat each other
of cause and effect uncertain
blind men asking the color of milk
no matter who's under Heaven
there's always a number of hues
Old Lady Chia with such a husband
Huang-Lao without a wife
the Wei boys were darlings
Miss Chung was a fright
is she walked west
I'd run east
wise men aren't voracious
the fool loves the furnace
his grain fields swallow others'
the bamboo grove's all his
he strains his arms after riches
gnashes his teeth spurring horse and slave on
he should look beyond the city gate
at the mound after mound below cedar and pine
they haggle over fish and meat
shoulder it home to feed their families
buy why do they take others' lives
to keep themselves alive
this isn't heaven-bound karma
simply waste for hell
when Hsu-liu says let's dig
they'll know it wans't right
some people take cedar
and call it sandalwood
myriads look for the Way
how few reach Nirvana
they abandon gold and shoulder straw
fool others and themselves
gathering sand together
it's hard to make a ball
steam sand to make rice
when you're thirsty dig a well
polish a brick with all your might
will it ever be a mirror
the Buddha said we're basically equal
we all have the Truly-So nature
just figure it out yourself
you don't have to struggle in vain
they look into worldy affairs
have to know them in all detail
take nothing lightly
love to gain an edge
defending themselves bad becomes good
attacking othere right becomes wrong
so know these vulgar mouths
it's all his fault behind his back
but hot and cold I'll feel for myself
I don't trust the lips of slaves
undone poor scholars
hungry and cold to extremes
out of work you like to write poems
scribbling with the strength of your hearts
but who collects a nobody's words
you may as well save your sighs
write them on gruel cakes
and even mongrels won't bite [which even begging dogs do not eat [CA]]
for an image of life and death
just look at ice and water
water freezes into ice
ice melts back into water
what dies is bound to live
what lives will surely die
ice and water don't harm each other
life and death as a pair are fine
Recalling the days of my youth
off hunting toward P'ing Ling
an envoy's job wasn't my wish
immortals weren't my fancy
I rode a white horse on the wing
flushed hares and loosed a falcon
suddenly now adrift
who'll show a white mane pity
I rested below a deep forest
and lived as a farmer
I planted myself upright
when I spoke I didn't flatter
I treasured myself but reflected no jade
trusted others and then found jewels
hoe could I join drifting and swirling
faraway ducks on the waves
you don't need to attack others' faults
you don't need to flaunt your own virtues
do whatever works
whatever doesn't don't
trials are great when rewards are heavy
consideration is shallow when words are deep
think about what you hear
children must see for themselves
rich men gathered in a lofty hall
how the colored lanterns blazed
then someone without a candle
thought he'd settle nearby
unexpectedly evicted
he went back to hide in the dark
would one more person have ruined the light
strange grudging extra rays
a brilliant scholar around
strains to fathom murky writings
his three tips stand alone
in the six arts he's unique
his air is breathlessly different
quintessence above the herd
but not seeing the meaning write there
he chases distinctions all over
the layered bloom of hills and streams
kingfisher shades locked up in the clouds
mountain mist whisks my cotton cap wet
dew soaks sedge-grass clothes
my feet wear wandering shoes
my hand holds an old vine staff
again I look beyond the dusty world
no more to that land of dreams
my scrolls are filled with the poems of masters
my jugs overflow with the wine of the sages
walking I love to watch buffalo calves
sitting I don't go far
and when frost or dew enters thatched eaves
and moonlight lights a crockery sill
I sip a couple of cups
and hum a couple of poems
Mister Shih had two sons
they pressed Ch'i and Ch'u with arts
in arms or letters each readied himself
they attached themselves for jobs
Mister Meng asked for instriuction
Mister Shih's sons taught hsi
in Ch'in and Wei they were feilures
out of step they were teeth that don't bite
mandarin ducks staying the night
a hen along with a drake
carry flowers and eat them together
preen their feathers and follow each other
frolic off in the mist
lodge on a sandy shore
content with native joys
they don't usurp the phoenix's lake
some people flaunt their practices
their talents surpass Confucius and Chou
look at their heads in a trance
see their bodies all clods
pulled by a rope the won't budge
stuck with an awl they won't move
just like Lord Yang's crane
a pity to be so dumb
I carried books and a hoe when I was young
living with my elder brothers
somehow I met their reproach
I was even disdained by my wife
so I left the land of red dust
now I roam and love to read
who'll spare a dipper of water
to sustain a fish in a rut
changes are inexhaustible
births and deaths never stop
a bird-body in the mire
a dragon-self on a peak
in a chaotic world a mountain sheep
in peaceful times a great horse
last time around a rich man
this time through a poor clerk
my script and decisions aren't feeble at all
but an unseemly body gets no post
examiners expose me with a twist
wash away the dirt and search for my sores
of course it depends of Heaven's will
but this year I'll try again
if a blind man shoots for a sparrow's eye
he just might score a hit
a poor donkey is short by a foot
a rich dog has three inches extra
you divide poverty unequally
or halve wealth and hardship
and once you let the donkey fill up
you cause the dog to starve
I've measured this for you carefully
it just makes me depressed
Mister Liu is eighty-two
Sister-in-Law eighteen
husband and wife share a hundred years
and love but a a love perverse
playing with a scepter is Tiger
throwing around tiles Butterball
whenever you see withered willows sprout
they're slain by girls from the blue
a guest of great hunger and cold
born to be different form fishes and beasts
stays alive beneath temples and rocks
often cries off the road
for days he imagines food in vain
all winter he knows no coat
he only packs a bunch of weeds
along with five pints of chaff
whose wine shop is this aglow
their wine's so rich and strong
lovely prominent pennants
and apparently the measure's fair
why then doesn't it sell
their place has too many currs
if a lad comes in to buy
they snap and away he runs
look at this vulgar place
demons together with worthies
I say they're one big bunch
but you think they're not kin
foxes borrow a lion's mien
and claim the disguise is real
when lead ore enters the furnace
the month when flatlanders come up for air
who'd like to share a jug of wine
I've put some mountain fruit out
and a few wine cups around
with rushes for mats
and banana leaves as plates
drunk and my chin propped up
Sumeru is just a pea
who's this would-be great
always coming to check South Hall
surely over thirty
he's tried now four or five times
in his purse no green beetles
in his pack yellow scrolls
coming to a place to eat
he dares not even look
it's a waste visiting sky-high pavilions
vain climbing hundred-foot towers
nursing your health you'll still die young
tempted by books you won't be enfeoffed
you don't need to follow a yellow mouth
and why should you loathe a white head
if you can't be straight as an arrow
just don't be crooked as a hook
clouds and mountains piled to the blue
remote and primeval it's no promenade
far off I see the lone toad clear and bright
nearby I hear a flock of birds talking chirp chirp
an old man I perch on a green ridge alone
small house no career I manage a white head
but sight that today and the years gone by
are mindless like the rivers flowing east
far and near crowd the rich and honored
just because of more rice and money
flesh and bones leave the poor and lowly
not because they're less than brothers
hard pressed they go back home
the Center of the Worthies hasn't opened yet
it's idle walking Red Bird Street
wearing out leather soles
I met a foolish man
who managed to wed a few wives
and raise eight or nine sons
all as neat as you please
but those of age are now draftees
and his property's not what it was
with yellow cork for a donkey's crupper
you know there's pain behind
the new grain still unripe
the old grain already gone
I went to borrow a quart or so
and stood anxious outside the door
he man came out and said ask his wife
the wife came out and said ask her man
misers don't help the needy
and wealth just makes them dumber
of very funny affairs
I'll briefly mention a few
Lord Chang was a rich showy flower
Mencius a poor bent axel
as long as the dwarves are full
who cares if Fangshuo starves
many people sing the Songs of Pa
nobody knows White Snow
when an old man takes a young wife
she won't endure his white hair
when an old woman weds a young man
he won't love her yellow face
but when an old man takes an old wife
neither will turn form the other
and when a young girl weds a young man
both will show their love
a graceful handsome youth
well-versed in classics and histories
everyone calls him sir
they all address him scholar
but he hasn't been able to get a position
and he doesn't know how to handle a plough
winter he throws on a tattered robe
this is how books fool us
when I can't stand the stirring of birds
I lie in my grass hut then
while the cherry's still dark
and the willow just fuzzy
the rising sun mouths a blue ridge
clearing clouds wash a green lake
who'd think of leaving the dusty rut
and heading south up Cold Mountain
p.note: Cherries not being pink, this seems to be an early case of 紅 referring to a colour that must be studied. 待考

p.seg: yesterday carries me off
to such lovely scene
above was a path of peach and plum
below was a shore of flag
and then someone in twilled sheer silks
kingfisher plumes inside
we met we almost called
we looked but coundn't speak
don't stay down my friend
try husbandry if you're broke
raise a single cow
and she'll beget five calves
calves beget calves too
numbers without end
to tell Lord Chu to T'ao
you're just as rich as him
this person is so unsure
but choosing a home needs thought
the South has many plagues
the North harsh wind and frost
wild spots can't be settled
poison rivers are hard to drink
spirit go back home
eat the mulberries in my yard
last night I dreamt I went home
and saw my wife at her loom
she stopped the shuttle in thought
then raised it without any strength
I called and she turned to look
but she no longer knew me
I guess we'd apart too many years
and my temples weren't their old color
man's life doesn't fill a hundred
but he harbors thousand-year cares
as soon as he's well enough
he worries about sons and grandsons
down he looks at the rice sprout patch
and up the tops of mulberry trees
if he dropped his scales in the Eastern Sea
he wouldn't rest till they hit bottom
there's someone around
as dense as a block of wood
he speaks without understanding
and says he hasn't a care
but ask him the Way and he doesn't know
ask for the Buddha he won't even look
discover in detail
a vast expense of woe
when master Tung was young
he was in and out of the palace
his shirt was gosling yellow
his looks and ways were a picture
he rode a snow-footed horse
flying past the red dust rose
on-lookers filled the roadside
who on earth was that
who on earth was that
a man greatly hated
his foolish mind usually vexed
earthly vision drunk and dim
he doesn't bow to the buddhas he sees
doesn't give to the monks he meets
only knows how to cut big steaks
otherwise he's helpless
the body is a person's root
the mind is the root's stem
the mind mustn't stray from the root
when it does it ends the root's life
still unable to avoid this disaster
why be too lazy to look the mirror
if you don't read the Diamond Sutra
you'll make bodhisattvas sick
Old Chung north of town
had plenty of meat and wine
the time Old Chung's wife died
mourners filled the hall
Old Chung died himself
and not one person cried
they swallowed his meat and wine
but had such cold insides
when idiots read my poems
they don't understand and sneer
when average people read them
they reflect and say they're deep
when worthies read my poems
they reflect with full-face grins
Yang Hsiu was young woman (!!!!!!!?????)
one look and he knew mystery
there may be stingy people
but I'm not the stingy sort
my clothes aren't lined so I'm dressed to dance
out of wine I get drunk on song
try to keep your stomach full
but don't wear your two feet out
when brambles work through your skull
you'll repent that day
my path went through an old cemetery
the tears and sighs long gone
yellow guts forced their way through graves
white bones stuck out of coffins
urn and vases leaned about
no hat pin or tablet moved
then the wind came stirring
ashes and dust all over
sunset I went down the western hills
the grass and trees were bright
but there were hazy places too
where pines and vines conspired
and lots of tigers crouched
bristling at my sight
and me without a knife
didn't I tremble in fright
once we appear we're harassed
by more than one affair
and we can't give up the customs
so we chase each other around
I just mourned Hsu-wu's death
today went to Liu-san's funeral
day after day without a break
this is why I grieve
if pleasures come be happy
occasions shouldn't be missed
though they say one hundred years
who fills thirty-thousand days
lodged in the world an instant
don't chirp and chatter about money
the Classic of Piety's final chapter
lays out the end in detail
sitting alone I keep slipping away
far off with the cares of my heart
clouds wander by the mountainside
wind rushes out the valley
gibbons swing through the trees
birds call through the forest
time swishes past my temples
the year leaves me old with regrets
a man with a a good head and belly
versed in all six arts
south he's driven north
west he's driven east
forever adrift like duchweed
never at rest he's tangle-afly
who is he you ask
his surname's Poor his name's Nil
if another excels accept him
if he doesn't excel don't
if you excel there's room for others
if you don't there's none for you
loving the adept consoling the inept
a disciple of Goodness finds his place
I urge you to follow Tzu Chang's motto
and ignore Pu Shang's advice
pettiness really gets petty
men's hearts aren't the same
Old Yin laughed at Old Liu
Old Liu laughed at Old Yin
why did they laugh at each other
both travelled a treacherous course
racing higher and higher with loaded carts
they spilled and both were ruined
those days when I had money
I always lent it to you
and now you're fed and warm
and see me but don't share
you should recall when you were in need
you were like now with hopes
possession's a turn-taking business
I hope you weigh this well
man lives a hundred years
and the Buddha preached a twelvefold canon
but compassion is like a wild deer
and anger is like a tame dog
you can't drive a tame dog away
a wild deer prefers to run
if you want to tame your monkey mind
listen to the lion's roar
I'll tell you several things
that'll make you think I'm wise
completely broke don't sell your house
as soon as you're rich buy land
without a roof there's no escape
on a barge there's no sleep
these words hoping everyone sees
I've hung on the sunny eastside
plenty mysteries on Cold Mountain
climbers all get scared
the moon shines and water sparkles
the wind blows and grass rustles
snow turns to flowers on barren plum trees
clouds become leaves on snags
touched by rain they begin to revive
unless it's sunny you can't get through
a tree grew here before the woods
its age is twice as great
its roots have been twisted by hill and valley
its leaves been turned by the wind and frost
everyone laughs at its withered outside
no one cares about its beautiful core
but when the bark's been stripped away
what's left is just what's real
there's a naked bug on Cold Mountain
its body is white and its head is black
its hands hold two scrolls
the Way and The Power
when it stops it installs neither kettle nor stove
when it travels it packs no clothes
but always it grips the Swords of Wisdom
ready to strike troublesome foes
some people fear a white head
they can't let a red cord go
seek immortality in vain through drugs
scrounge every root and bud
several years without success
infatuated angered distressed
the hunter throws on a monk's robe
but it's not meant for him
before a triffle poor
today I'm utterly broke
whatever I try doesn't work out
every road's a treadmill
my legs buckle in the mud
my belly aches at the shrine
since I lost that calico cat
rats surround my rice jar
I see people in this world
dignified and fond of form
not repaying their parents' kindness
square-inches of the lowest sort
piling up debts to others
not repenting till they've got hooves
begrudging their families everything
not supporting their parents
brothers like enemies
minds forever depressed
remembering when they were young
asking the gods to make them mature
and now they're unfilial sons
the world's average sort
they buy meat and eat it alone
wipe their lips and say they're fine
ramble on about themselves
intelligent uselessly
the ox head's angry eyes glare
when he sees his time is up
he chooses a Buddha and burns fine joss
picks a monks and pledges support
but when arhats beg at his door
he drives the lazy monks off
unaware of the unengaged man
who has never had any form
he bestows on famous monks
alms of the paltry sort
while on dharma masters of rivers and clouds
on their heads he sets horns
if you don't have an impartial mind
no wise ones will descend
fools and sages all together
you' d better stop grabbing form
precious heavenly something
standing off by itself
looked for can't be seen
comes and goes but not through doors
crowded it's in a square-inch
stretched it's everywhere
whoever doesn't trust it
meets without accord
